questions.question: Why are residual connections critical in transformer blocks?
choices: They make the code run faster
They prevent gradient vanishing in deep networks by allowing gradients to flow directly
They reduce the number of parameters
They make the output more accurate
questions.explanation: Residual connections (adding input back after each sub-layer) provide a direct path for gradients to flow, preventing them from vanishing in deep networks.

questions.question: In a transformer block, what is the correct order of operations?
choices: Layer Norm -> Self-Attention -> Residual -> Layer Norm -> Feed-Forward -> Residual
questions.explanation: The correct order is: Layer Norm -> Self-Attention -> Add input (residual) -> Layer Norm -> Feed-Forward -> Add previous output (residual).

questions.question: What does Layer Normalization do in a transformer block?
choices: Scales and shifts activations to stabilize training
questions.explanation: Layer normalization normalizes activations across the feature dimension, stabilizing training by ensuring consistent scales across layers.
